doc.title: Bley Carla — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Shelly Manne and Bud Shank on the West Coast
summary: She admires Shelly Manne as drummer and listener and first heard cool jazz at a Bud Shank concert.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Did you encounter any of the musicians on the West Coast like Shelly Manne or Conte Candoli or folks like that?

We were just talking about Shelly Manne yesterday. What a wonderful drummer and what an incredible listener. And what a great raconteur, you called me earlier, he sure could get some things together, you know, and then he had his own band there opening for all his favorite bands that he’d bring from the East, it was just great. I really liked him a lot. But the rest of the bands, I remember going to a Bud Shank concert and hearing cool jazz for the first time. And I thought, wow that is cool. I think I like the hot stuff a little better. But then later on the cool was more, I was more able to understand it. It required more reflection and patience, and you couldn’t just be impatient and listen to it.
